classification.difficultyReason: Recognise that reaching 60 implies reaching 50 and use that nesting to turn two birth-based survival probabilities into a conditional ratio. Joe's separate probability requires a direct complement.

content.prompt:
In a certain population over a period of time, it was found that the probability $P(Y)$ that a newborn reaches age $Y$ is

$$\begin{aligned}P(50)&=0.922\\P(60)&=0.848\\P(70)&=0.714\\P(80)&=0.476\end{aligned}$$

children.label: a
children.prompt: What is the probability of a 50-year-old person from this population reaching the age of 60? Give your answer to 2 decimal places.

answer.worked:
Anyone who reaches 60 has already reached 50.

$$\begin{align*}P(\text{reaches 60}\mid\text{reaches 50})&=\frac{P(60)}{P(50)}\\P(\text{reaches 60}\mid\text{reaches 50})&=\frac{0.848}{0.922}\\P(\text{reaches 60}\mid\text{reaches 50})&\approx 0.92\quad\text{(2 d.p.)}\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: Joe the Farmer just turned 70 and has a $0.15$ chance of dying within the next 10 years. What is the probability that Joe lives to see his 80th birthday?

answer.worked:
Reaching age 80 and dying before age 80 are complementary outcomes for Joe.

$$\begin{align*}P(\text{Joe reaches 80})&=1-0.15\\P(\text{Joe reaches 80})&=0.85\end{align*}$$
